headlines.title: Elizabeth Holmes to be transferred to a halfway house
headlines.description: Elizabeth Holmes, who was convicted of fraud for siphoning hundreds of millions of dollars from several high-profile investors, is scheduled to be transferred from a low-security federal prison to a halfway house next year, according to one of her victims. Holmes, 42, defrauded investors of millions through Theranos, the failed blood-testing company that she founded. She was sentenced in 2022 to 11 years and three months in prison. She and her business partner Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani were ordered to pay 12 victims a total of $452 million in restitution. Holmes has been serving that sentence at a low-security prison in Bryan, Texas. The halfway house will provide her greater freedom. Alan Eisenman, one of her victims, said she is to be transferred to the Austin Transitional Center, a halfway house in Del Valle, an unincorporated community that borders Austin, Texas. The Department of Justice is required by law to notify victims of crime of case developments through letters and emails. Scott Taylor, a spokesperson for the Bureau of Prisons, said he could not provide details of Holmes’ confinement, including release plans. Taylor cited safety, security and a Bureau of Prisons policy that says such information can’t be released until after an individual arrives at their designated institution. Eisenman, an early Theranos investor who testified at Holmes’ trial, said he received a message from the Justice Department’s victim notification system Wednesday saying the halfway house transfer would occur in August 2027. Eisenman, a retired financial planner from Texas, invested about $1.2 million with his family in the failed blood-testing company beginning in 2006. He was the smallest investor among a list of high-profile, well-monied investors who included Australian media mogul Rupert Murdoch. Eisenman was unhappy to hear of the planned transfer. “Seems like a gift,” he told NBC News. Movies Sep 7 Elizabeth Holmes Jul 11, 2023 Holmes owes Eisenman and his wife, Sherrie, almost $150,000 out of a total of $452 million in restitution for all victims of her crimes, according to a court document. So far, he has “not received a penny” from Holmves, he told NBC News. “She was a liar back in 2006,” Eisenman said, “and she’s a liar today.” Eisenman said he hoped Holmes would remain in prison through her scheduled release date of Feb. 22, 2030, after some reductions in the sentence. In March, a judge cut Holmes’ sentence from 135 months to 123 months. According to a court document, the judge agreed with Holmes that she did not personally cause “substantial financial hardship” to her victims. The government had tried to prevent a reduction of her prison time, arguing that Holmes has not accepted responsibility for her crimes, paid minimal restitution and “has the opportunity to reoffend,” according to a court filing. The government told the court that Holmes has continued to tell national media she intends to resume a career in healthcare technology after her release and has been advising her romantic partner on fundraising for his startup, a company that has similarities to Theranos, the court document states. Eisenman added that he’s against Holmes receiving any form of presidential clemency. She filed for a commutation of her sentence last year. It remains pending. Holmes’ attorney from her trial did not respond to a phone message from NBC News requesting comment. ABC News first reported her pending release to the halfway house. Walter Pavlo, president of Prisonology LLC consulting firm, said a combination of factors could have helped reduce the time Holmes is spending in prison and at the halfway house. Those include a change on sentencing guidelines, good conduct time, possible participation in programs that slice time off her sentence if successfully completed and laws governing time she would spend in a halfway house and home confinement. Pavlo said inmates who report to halfway houses can work, have a phone and drive to religious services or shop for things they need and can earn passes for weekends at home. On its website, the Bureau of Prisons states that inmates at halfway houses are given counseling, job placement and other programs and services to help rebuild community ties. The BOP site states it monitors inmates’ activities, requires sign out and conducts head counts. Also, inmates “ordinarily” are expected to work 40 hours a week within 15 days of their arrival at the halfway house and some of their income pay for some of their stay at the halfway house, according to the BOP site. The news of Holmes’ impending move comes as a documentary about her is about to be released. The documentary by comedian Nathan Fielder and director Lance Oppenheim is based on Fielder living with her and her partner for several days before she entered prison in 2023. It recently made its debut at the Telluride Film Festival and is scheduled for full release next month. Eisenman said he also watched the latest trailer for the documentary, “You Can See Everything,” and plans to see it upon its release next month. His concern, he added, is whether it will portray Holmes as a sympathetic figure. “She’s obviously manipulative,” Eisenman said. “If people don’t see that, then they’re blind. She’s the most conniving person I’ve ever met.”
headlines.source: Suzanne Gamboa and Erik Ortiz | NBC News

headlines.title: San Jose restaurant owner frustrated by frequent break-ins
headlines.description: A San Jose restaurant owner who said she has lost count of how many times burglars have struck her business is calling on the city to do more. The owner of Mendoza’s Restaurant, located on McKee Road near Regional Medical Center, walked into work Wednesday morning to find broken glass. The owner said this time the burglars did not take anything because there was nothing of value. The owner is tired of the constant break-ins and the costs that come with repairing broken glass and equipment. She reports the break-ins to police and said officers come by to ask questions and take pictures, but she said she never hears of any arrests. headlines.title: Walmart settles for $16 million over expired goods on California shelves
headlines.description: Walmart Inc. has agreed to settle a civil lawsuit brought by seven California counties for $16 million over allegedly keeping baby formula and medication on shelves past their expiration dates, the Solano County District Attorney’s Office said Wednesday. The suit, brought by Solano, Alameda, Sacramento, San Bernardino, San Joaquin, Sonoma and Yolo counties, found that the retail giant routinely sold expired products, including cough syrup, sunscreen and cosmetics. An investigation found no evidence anyone was physically harmed by the expired goods. Walmart was cooperative during the investigation, according to the district attorney’s office. “Parents should never have to worry that the infant formula or medications they purchase for their children are expired and potentially unsafe,” said Solano County District Attorney Krishna Abrams. The settlement “strengthens safeguards to prevent similar violations in the future,” Abrams said. As part of the settlement, Walmart is prohibited from selling baby formula and over the counter drugs past the use date in all California stores. The company was also ordered to implement a training program for employees to better identify expired goods and take them off shelves. Walmart will also pay over $15.7 million in penalties and $250,000 in fees.

headlines.title: Motorcyclist killed in collision with turning vehicle in Fremont
headlines.description: A man riding a motorcycle in Fremont Wednesday died after colliding with a vehicle that was making a turn in an intersection. The collision happened at about 1:40 p.m. at Hastings and Keats streets, the Fremont Police Department said in a statement. The motorcyclist was riding northbound on Hastings Street and was traveling through the intersection when he collided with a passenger vehicle that was making a left turn from Keats Street onto southbound Hastings Street, according to a preliminary investigation by the police department’s traffic unit. The motorcyclist was unresponsive when police and paramedics arrived. He was pronounced dead from his injuries at a local hospital. It marked the 10th fatal traffic collision in Fremont in 2026, according to the police department. The collision remained under investigation Wednesday. Anyone with information was asked to contact the Fremont Police Department Traffic Unit at 510-790-6760.

headlines.title: Crews clean up derelict boats in San Francisco Bay
headlines.description: A massive cleanup took place Thursday morning in the San Francisco Bay. Oakland, along with the help from other cities, began removing derelict boats along Oakland Estuary’s water ways. For some time, shipwrecks have been littering the shore of the East Bay. NBC Bay Area’s Bob Redell recaps the cleanup efforts in the video above.

headlines.title: Steph Curry visits East Oakland school, talks vision issue
headlines.description: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry visited Madison Park Academy Primary in East Oakland on Wednesday to discuss a personal health issue. Curry is battling the progressive eye condition keratoconus, which effects vision. He didn’t let the serious topic dampen the day, joining the students for a book distribution and basketball clinic, while sharing his personal mission to inspire children to overcome physical obstacles. Curry said the diagnosis caused him anxiety, but he’s learned to manage it. Steph Curry 17 hours ago Steph Curry Sep 23 Steph Curry reveals rare eye condition diagnosis during Warriors' dynasty run

headlines.title: Authorities search for missing person in the water in Antioch
headlines.description: Authorities said they are searching for a missing person in the water in Antioch Wednesday. Contra Costa Fire said they were dispatched to a report of a person in the water at around 6:16 p.m. at 1 Marina Plz in Antioch. Crews arrived on boats and rescued one person, who was then taken to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Authorities said there were reports of another person still in the water. Just before 10:30 p.m., the Coast Guard confirmed to NBC Bay Area the search is ongoing for the missing person.

headlines.title: Pedestrian struck, killed by vehicle in Richmond
headlines.description: A pedestrian was killed in a collision in Richmond on Thursday morning, according to police. Richmond police officers responded to the 2300 block of Maricopa Avenue, where they are investigating the fatal collision involving a vehicle and a pedestrian. Maricopa Avenue is expected to remain closed between 23rd and 24th streets for several hours while officers investigate. Drivers are being asked to avoid the area and use alternate routes. Additional information was not immediately available.

headlines.title: BART considers adding more surveillance cameras as part of safety push
headlines.description: BART leaders are looking at the impact of surveillance cameras across the transit system, with the possibility of adding more. BART officials say surveillance cameras, along with the agency’s new fare gates, have been instrumental in cutting down on crime. BART will ask its board to continue the surveillance already in place and add two new cameras — one at BART Police Department headquarters and another at the Union City at-grade pedestrian crossing. Closed-circuit television cameras are used extensively across BART to identify and prevent threats to people and property. According to BART, the cameras assisted with more than 3,700 video requests. More than 2,300 were for criminal investigations, more than 1,300 were for train car video and more than two dozen were for court subpoenas. BART police also produced 220 wanted-person bulletins using images from the cameras. The data comes as BART marks one year since new fare gates were installed at all 50 stations. BART says crime against riders has dropped 67%, while safety delays have been cut by nearly half. Officials also estimate the new gates have brought in roughly $10 million that would have otherwise been lost to fare evasion. BART riders surveyed say they are satisfied with the transit agency. The data comes as transit agencies, including BART, face a financial cliff. Voters are being asked to approve two ballot measures in November as BART faces a roughly $300 million budget deficit.

headlines.title: Meta bets big on new AI agent and glasses as Zuckerberg pushes back against doom
headlines.description: Meta is going all in on a consumer-friendly AI agent and pushing forward with AI-powered wearable devices during a moment in the industry when its CEO Mark Zuckerberg acknowledged it is a “wild time to be building.” At the company’s annual Connect conference on Wednesday, Zuckerberg opened his keynote address by saying “it’s no secret that people in the industry have a wide range of views about how the future is going to go.” But at Meta, he said, “we are optimists because we believe in people.” Zuckerberg has distanced himself and Meta from recent calls by rival companies for a coordinated slowdown in the development of advanced artificial intelligence, arguing that individual labs can and should ensure their technology is safe. “We believe that the best way to create a positive future for everyone is to put power in people’s hands,” he said at the conference. “We believe that empowering people is the source of prosperity in the world, that the highest purpose of superintelligence is creation and invention — not automation — and that the path to a safe future is to distribute this technology widely and create the right checks and balances, rather than concentrating it in the hands of just a few.” Zuckerberg has long said he believes wearable AI will eventually replace smartphones as the primary way people interact with technology. At the conference, the company unveiled a slew of updates to its smart glasses and virtual reality goggles, which let people control their interface using their voice, eyes and hand and finger movements. AI agent Muse is the ‘centerpiece’ of Meta’s vision Zuckerberg said that Meta’s recently launched agent Muse is the “centerpiece” of Meta’s hopeful outlook for the future of AI. Having an AI agent, which goes beyond chatbots in that it can act and perform tasks on a person’s behalf, has been a “sign of someone who is completely AI-pilled,” Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said at the conference. With Muse, Wang said, Meta is making agents more accessible and bringing “personal superintelligence” to everyone. With the help of a mascot for the agent that looks like a plush toy, Wang and senior leadership at Meta demonstrated different uses for the Muse in everyday life. Users will be able to have real-time voice conversations and video chats with their version of the agent, which can also be customized to look and sound unique. The agent can help users plan travel, book reservations, order groceries and complete other helpful tasks. Meta has partnered with companies like OpenTable, Spotify, Ticketmaster and more to help its agents complete these tasks. The company is working to bring Muse to its AI glasses lineup for hands-free access. Zuckerberg also said Meta is planning to release a keychain-like device that has the “whole Muse experience” packed into it, called Muse Charm, in time for the holidays in December. The palm-sized device will allow users to engage with a personal AI agent without using a phone, computer or smart glasses. Artificial intelligence Sep 23 Artificial intelligence Sep 16 New AI audio glasses and new updates to popular models Meta is launching an audio version of its more widely known smart glasses. The new product will let users listen to music, make calls and talk with an AI assistant — there’s just no screen, and no video recording, which has raised privacy concerns with some users recording people without permission. Called Ray-Ban Meta Audio, it will be available in October and the cost starts at $349. Meta is also building upon a previous feature that allowed glasses wearers to better hear a conversation in a noisy environment. Now, Zuckerberg said, a feature called hearing enhancement turns your glasses into an “FDA-cleared, over-the-counter hearing aid” that can “compensate for perceived mild to moderate hearing loss.” The feature will launch in the U.S. later this year and will be available to add to supported AI glasses for $150, or with a Meta One subscription. The Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses have been upgraded with new features, including improved cycling and transit navigation and a personalized hologram for video calls. The company is also offering more styles to appeal to a broader range of people and says it will have more than 100 different options across its Ray-Ban, Oakley, and Meta Glasses by the end of the year. The glasses will also be available in more countries, including Turkey, Hong Kong and the Philippines. The newest generation of the classic Ray-Ban Meta glasses is also now available, with what the company touts as a slimmer, sleeker design and increased battery life, among other upgrades. The Generation 3 models are available now with prices starting at $449. Virtual reality gets a makeover with Meta VR Glasses The most drastic update announced at the conference is to the company’s VR device, now called Meta VR Glasses. That is because the previous bulky headset has been replaced by a set of glasses, which weigh about 3.5 ounces, or roughly as much as a deck of cards. In comparison, the Meta Quest 3, which launched in 2023, weighs about five times that much. The difference feels similar to that between scuba diving and swimming goggles. While they are significantly lighter and more sleek than VR predecessors, the glasses require a wired connection to an external puck for battery, storage and compute. Instead of controllers or a neural wristband that past headsets or glasses required, the VR glasses use an eye-tracking camera and sensor that essentially lets your eyes be the computer cursor and your fingers the mouse clicker. If you want to open an app, for instance, you look at it and use hand and finger gestures, or use voice commands to talk to the Meta AI agent. In a demo at its Menlo Park, California, headquarters on Tuesday, Meta showed off entertainment and work offerings on the glasses, including sports events and concerts that replicate the experience of having courtside or front-row seats. A new feature called “VR Enhanced Cinema,” meanwhile, seeks to immerse viewers in the movie by transforming their surroundings beyond the screen into a virtual world inspired by the movie, with dynamic effects, 3D visuals and spatial audio. Once the glasses launch, users will have access to more than 100 immersive live sports events from that courtside-like view, because of partnerships with ESPN, MLB, NBC Sports, TNT Sports and UFC. The glasses can also function as a gaming console, Meta said, and there will be more than 75 games at launch that users can play solely with hand gestures. The glasses can also be used for work. Users can conjure a virtual keyboard on any flat surface and use the display as their computer screen (or several screens) only they can see. For even more of a robust setup, users will be able to connect their Mac or Windows PC to seamlessly transition onto these screens, and bring their own keyboard and mouse. The VR glasses, unlike headsets of the past, will let wearers see their desk setup and surroundings while they work. One of Zuckerberg’s live demos of the night also showed off the glasses’ ability to use hologram technology to project a photorealistic digital version of a person, including their real-time expressions and reactions, for hands-free video calling. The VR glasses will launch in the spring of 2027 and cost $1,300.
headlines.source: Kaitlyn Huamani and Barbara Ortutay | The Associated Press

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot and descriptions from the secretary of state: Proposition 1: Authorizes bonds for housing affordability programs Proposition 2: Increases state’s rainy day fund Proposition 3: Provides permanent funding for schools and healthcare by extending existing tax on high incomes Proposition 4: Repeals prohibition against public funding of election campaigns. Proposition 5: Changes recall election process for statewide officers. Proposition 37: Creates loan program for middle-income buyers of qualified new homes. Proposition 38: Authorizes bonds for immunology medical research. Proposition 39: Prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification. Proposition 40: Imposes one-time tax on certain taxpayers. Proposition 41: Prohibits new state taxes that exclude revenues from state spending limit. Requires audits for new state special taxes. Proposition 42: Prohibits new state personal property taxes and certain retroactive state taxes. Proposition 43: Limits voters’ ability to raise revenues for local government services. Proposition 44: Requires community health clinics spend 90% of revenue on program services. Proposition 45: Modifies environmental review for certain projects. Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax (not assigned) Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: San Francisco Fleet Week 2026: Events, schedules, what to know
headlines.description: It’s that time of year again. San Francisco Fleet Week is back. The fall tradition will be highlighted by the Blue Angels screaming across the skies, but there are plenty of other events to experience. Check out the guide below to learn more about Fleet Week events. What is San Francisco Fleet Week? San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual celebration of the nation’s sea services. A multi-day air show, parade of ships and ship tours highlight the weeklong festivities. “San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual public event that honors the contributions of the men and women of the United States Armed Forces while advancing cooperation and knowledge among civilian- and military-based Humanitarian Assistance personnel,” a statement on the event’s website reads. When is San Francisco Fleet Week 2026? Fleet Week is scheduled to take place Sunday, Oct. 4 through Monday, Oct. 12. San Francisco Fleet Week Air Show Head to a location along San Francisco Bay between the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz to catch a thrilling aerial show featuring the Blue Angels, a United Airlines 777, and much more. When: 12 p.m. – 4 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 9, Saturday, Oct. 10 and Sunday, Oct. 11 Lineup and schedule: Stay tuned for detailed information on the airshow lineup and schedule Where: Ticketed seating located at the Marina Green in San Francisco Tickets: Air show tickets are available via the San Francisco Fleet Week website Note: Gates open at 10 a.m. on Friday and 11 a.m. on Saturday and Sunday Bay Area Jan 16 San Francisco Sep 3 San Francisco Fleet Week Parade of Ships Set your eyes on the water near the Golden Gate Bridge to catch the fleet of ships arriving in the Bay, escorted by a San Francisco Fire Department boat shooting water into the air. When: 11 a.m. – 12 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 9 Where: San Francisco Bay waterfront (the parade can be seen from locations along the water between the Golden Gate Bridge and the Bay Bridge) San Francisco Fleet Week Ship Tours Climb aboard various ships to see what it’s like to be a sailor in the U.S. Navy and U.S. Coast Guard. The visiting ships will be announced in late September.
